title: P1: provide governed conflict-resolution successor route
rawUserRequest: Execute the existing #709 corrective from current origin/main. Add the only governed route for an active Work Item whose ai-synchronize-work-item attempt conflicts: preserve source active evidence and any authorized checkpoint, bind the exact conflict context and user authority, and create a clean current-main successor without manual rebase, stash, archive rewrite, or a duplicate GitHub Issue. The user authorizes automatic execution and requires that authority to be recorded in every Work Item Contract.

declaredIntent.summary: Make an active synchronization conflict an auditable transition to a current-main successor rather than a manual Git operation or a lifecycle dead end.

outOfScope: Manual rebase, merge, stash, force-push, archive rewrite, or cross-worktree modification of the conflicted source Work Item.
Publishing a release, merging a PR, changing provider state, or deleting branches outside this Work Item lifecycle.
Weakening Start Receipt, ownership, synchronization, or PR-audit checks.

sources.reason: User-authorized existing corrective Issue and acceptance boundary.
Current fail-closed synchronization and automatic rebase-abort behavior.
Immutable Start Receipt and synchronization-history validation boundary.
Canonical current synchronization instruction to extend.

riskAssessment.reason: A malformed conflict transition could lose active evidence, authorize a manual conflict resolution, or bind a successor to the wrong source/checkpoint.

reasons: Synchronization and successor identity alter lifecycle/ownership evidence.

executionDecision.reason: The existing Issue, preserved #663 conflict evidence, current-main successor requirement, user authority, and executable verification plan are explicit.

preReviewWarnings: The source Work Item must remain untouched after its failed synchronization except for the narrowly defined receipt; the successor must start from current main and retain no source code by hidden Git replay.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A failed active synchronization conflict produces a fail-closed, append-only receipt binding the source Work Item, source branch/head/checkpoint, target base, conflict context, repository Issue, and recorded human authority without changing source Contract, Summary, Start Receipt, or archive evidence.

A dedicated successor can be initialized only from the verified current remote default branch and only when its Contract records the exact bound conflict receipt; stale, forged, mismatched, incomplete, foreign, or replayed receipt data fails closed.

The route never executes manual conflict resolution, stash, force-push, archive mutation, provider mutation, merge, release, or source branch deletion; the source remains auditable and blocked/quarantined until its successor lifecycle closes.
Source Make targets, installed template/runtime catalog, tests, and canonical documentation expose the same fail-closed behavior.
Focused red/green tests, full required quality, Finish/archive, clean committed PR audit, hosted CI, merge, and governed closure pass.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An active Work Item synchronization creates an authorized checkpoint and then conflicts with the verified remote default branch.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The rebase is automatically aborted, source evidence remains unchanged except for the already-authorized checkpoint, and a bound conflict receipt can be opened without Git conflict resolution.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Extend a real Git fixture to force a conflict, compare source evidence bytes/head, and validate the receipt contents.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A successor is requested from a stale base, foreign Issue, forged receipt, mismatched source head, or a non-current branch.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The command fails before it writes successor lifecycle evidence or changes source state.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add focused negative tests that vary each bound field and assert no receipt/successor write occurs.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A valid receipt is consumed by a dedicated successor started from the live current main baseline.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The successor Contract binds the source conflict receipt and its current base; the source remains quarantined and cannot be silently treated as synchronized.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Use an end-to-end repository fixture covering source conflict, receipt creation, successor start, and receipt validation.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An installed strict adopter needs the same conflict successor command.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Its Makefile and copied runtime expose the command and reject absent runtime dependencies.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Extend Makefile, installer, and installed-runtime parity tests.

guidelines: Preserve the conflicted source Work Item evidence byte-for-byte and make every new transition receipt append-only and digest-bound.
Use executable negative and positive tests for conflict, stale, forged, and current-main successor cases; documentation alone is insufficient.
Keep source, installed template, and runtime command surfaces in parity.
Do not treat a conflict transition receipt as authority to merge, publish, delete branches, or close a Work Item.

intent.problem: #663 demonstrated that ai-synchronize-work-item correctly creates an authorized checkpoint and automatically aborts a conflicting rebase, but leaves no governed continuation to the now-current main baseline. #711 consequently cannot use the new post-archive recovery capability without a prohibited manual Git operation.
constraints: Keep source Work Item evidence and checkpoint auditable.
No manual rebase, merge, stash, force-push, or archive rewrite.
Successor must originate at verified current origin/main.
Bind repository Issue and the user's standing automation authority.
Do not create a new GitHub Issue for this known lifecycle defect.
intent.rationale: A narrow, receipt-bound conflict-to-successor route turns a safe abort into a recoverable governance state while retaining the one-Work-Item-per-branch/PR rule for the actual delivery.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: User gave standing authorization to execute the full plan automatically and record it in every Contract, including the necessary existing #709 conflict-successor repair.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff and restore related tests and docs.
